summary.name: Health information technology
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia article describing health information technology (HIT): the use of computing and communications technology in health care, covering EHRs, CPOE, regulation, and policy.
use_cases: Understanding how electronic health records are adopted and regulated
Researching medication error reduction with CPOE
Learning about US federal incentives for EHR adoption
Reviewing risks of technology-induced medical errors
summary.what_it_does: This is an encyclopedia overview, not a software product. It defines health information technology and health informatics and describes the main HIT categories, including electronic health records, computerized provider order entry, dispensing and administration technologies, and health information exchange. It summarizes policy history such as the HITECH Act incentives, the FDASIA-based risk-based regulatory framework, and the HL7 FHIR standard. It also discusses adoption barriers, medication-error evidence, and technology-induced errors.
notable: Covers US policy history including HITECH incentives and the FDASIA risk-based regulatory framework
Describes the HL7 FHIR open standard for interoperability
Discusses technological iatrogenesis and risks of CPOE
caveats: Encyclopedia article with no software to download or use; the page is not a tool
Some figures and claims are dated (mostly 2004 to 2015 era sources)
